correctness.rationale: Each antipodal pair of vertices has a supporting normal. Cap-to-cap pairs contribute n^2, the regular-polygon planar support candidates provide exactly 2n same-layer pairs for odd order and n for even order. Exact normals for the 2n triangular facets yield n opposite triangle pairs for odd order but none for even order. Applying the explicitly cited local defect theorem gives delta = 2n-1+5n for odd and delta=2n-1 for even, and the definition determines B. The supporting normals exist for every positive height; invertible anisotropic scaling preserves antipodality. A separate solver reproduced all 39 count equalities for n=3 through 15, but the full theorem is proved analytically, not inferred from samples.

value.rationale: The exact pair counts for a natural family of right regular antiprisms reveal the sharp contrast between odd, centrally symmetric members with n opposite pairs of lateral triangular facets and even members with none. This produces an aspect-ratio-independent gap of 5n in a natural second-homology rank relative to the even-formula baseline, and distinguishes antiprisms from polygonal prism results. The entire pair census is more informative than a single small computational invariant.
